title: RESUME.json
description: The artifact a resuming agent reads. Sealed for WP-024 before any fixture existed. Every leaf declares which of the four categories it belongs to, because the categories carry different invalidation rules: observations expire on observation age, assertions on their own terms, computations on their inputs, and constants never.

source_sha.description: The commit this state was derived from. An agent compares it against observed.main_sha; a mismatch makes the whole artifact stale regardless of any other field.

static.description: Never expires. Constants do not need an invalidation rule.

observed.description: Facts read from git, the API or the filesystem. Each carries its own observation time and freshness, because one unavailable API call must not silently downgrade the rest.

asserted.description: Human judgement. Not derivable, and it rots differently: an assertion goes stale when the world it references moves, not when a clock runs out - which is why revoked_at exists alongside valid_until.

oneOf.description: null means NONE_SAFE. There is no safe action.

next_action.description: Exactly one, or null. A list would let a reader choose, which is the failure this artifact exists to prevent.

freshness.description: The WORST freshness among critical inputs, never an average. One UNKNOWN critical observation makes the artifact UNKNOWN.

declared_non_coverage.description: What this artifact does not establish. Present so that absence of a stop condition is not read as absence of risk.

value.description: null is permitted and means the observation could not be made. It must be paired with freshness UNKNOWN.

source.description: How it was obtained, e.g. 'git rev-parse HEAD' or 'GET /repos/:o/:r/pulls?state=open'.

issuer.description: Who made this claim. An assertion with no issuer cannot be revoked by anyone.

valid_until.description: null means it does not expire on a clock. It can still be revoked.
